brief: Bernstein reran its data center credibility model for October, scoring all 8,858 North American projects in the Aterio database on development stage, tenant quality, developer track record and state politics. Of 586 GW announced, under construction or land-banked, only 199 GW (34%) is credible; 387 GW is "bragawatts." That ratio has barely moved across three updates (33%, 35%, 34%) even as the gross pipeline grew from 411 GW to 586 GW, so new announcements keep adding mostly non-credible capacity. Stage of development is the single largest filter (198 GW cut), ahead of tenant quality (113 GW), developer history (48 GW) and state politics (28 GW), so tenant credit risk is a bigger threat to the pipeline than the election-driven state moratoria Wall Street is modeling this week. Tenant risk centers on OpenAI (0.50 credibility multiplier, same as Groq) and Oracle (cut again to 0.75) because Oracle is the counterparty on Stargate. Politically, Texas, Pennsylvania, Virginia and New York now sit at a 0.70 floor post-election. Behind-the-meter power is growing fastest but is least credible: only 4% of operating capacity runs on-site. Bernstein's framing is that the 387 GW that was never going to be built is what triggered the political backlash now threatening the 199 GW that is real.
